about: Slice 15: the frigate Commonwealth's textures and wear (weathering.py, docs/shipkit-15). One card per surface: which of her materials it covers (by kind), how close a camera comes, the pattern's real size, the detail maps it draws, and what each of the texture loop's five levels (Tools/texloop/levels.json) looks like on her. Every material the build makes is in a card, in 'unweathered' with its reason, or in 'below_decks' (dressed as slices 12 to 14 land); weathering.dress() stops otherwise.
salt_note: she lives in salt water (Galveston's ship channel and offshore): rust, verdigris and the waterline's growth at the salt-water rate, not the lake's third (docs/texture-loop metal)

levels.L0: launched, autumn 1797: new paint glossy in linseed oil, bright salmon copper, yellow new pine and oak, the rigging fresh-tarred black and sticky, new buff canvas
levels.L1: her first cruise, a few months out: the paint's gloss softer and salt dried white under the ports, the copper browned, the deck holystoned pale, the tar dulled, the canvas a shade greyer
levels.L2: six years in commission, half kept (a working cruise, refitted between): faded chalky paint with rust and tar runs, the copper dark brown with green at the waterline, a grey deck, the rigging brown and rope-worn, sails dingy and patched
levels.L3: thirty years on, kept by a proud navy yard (a ship in ordinary kept smart, or a well-found old frigate): repainted, the deck holystoned white, the rigging re-tarred, the copper renewed brown; the oak's grain worn proud, the gilt renewed, every bright thing clean
levels.L4: twenty years laid up and neglected (a hulk): paint chalked and flaking to grey oak, rust and tar bleeding down the side, the copper green and lifting with weed and barnacles at the waterline, a black and green deck, the rigging grey and rotten, mildewed sails

paint.title: Oil paint on oak
paint.what: The side's black, the ochre band, the red inside the bulwarks and on the gun carriages, the figure and the window sashes' stone white: lamp black, yellow ochre, red ochre and white lead ground in linseed oil, brushed on the planking (her strakes are modelled, so the seams are the model's)
paint.closest_camera_note: from a boat alongside, or leaning on the rail
paint.pattern_note: her fastenings are at every frame (room and space 2 ft), one bolt or treenail row per strake; old oil paint alligators into cells a centimetre or so across

levels.L0: deep glossy black, a clean yellow ochre and a rich red, every brush stroke still wet-looking
levels.L1: the gloss softening; white salt dried in faint streaks under the ports and along the wales
levels.L2: faded and chalky (the black brownish grey, the ochre pale), rust runs from the fastenings, tar drips from above, scrapes along the wales
levels.L3: repainted over thirty years of coats: deep black, the grain and old coats showing through, touched up in glossier patches where it chafes, no salt, clean
levels.L4: chalked nearly grey, the paint alligatored and flaking to grey oak, rust and tar bleeding down in long runs, the seams opening

refs.note: black paint worn and scratched on planks

copper.title: Copper sheathing
copper.what: The bottom's copper sheets to the main wale's foot: sheets 4 ft by 14 in, laid in rows from aft forward with each row's seam half a sheet on from the last, lapped and nailed round their edges
copper.closest_camera_note: from a boat alongside at the waterline

levels.L0: bright new salmon-pink copper, each sheet a little different, the laps and nail rows crisp
levels.L1: browned within weeks: an even warm brown with a dull sheen, the laps and nail rows still crisp
levels.L2: dark chocolate brown with green verdigris streaks at the waterline and a slimy band
levels.L3: renewed sheet by sheet over the years: dark old sheets with brighter new ones let in among them, clean, no weed
levels.L4: green and black, sheets lifting at the laps, weed and barnacles in a broad band at the waterline

refs.note: copper browned (cuprite), the colour new sheathing takes in its first weeks

wood.title: Bare and oiled wood
wood.what: Unpainted oak (the waterways, rails, coamings, gratings, capstan, wheel, catheads' and anchors' stocks, the boats' oak), the elm blocks and deadeyes with their lignum vitae sheaves and pins, and the spars: scraped and oiled bright (with the period's tar and oil)
wood.closest_camera_note: the rail and the belaying pins at a hand's reach

levels.L0: new oak's warm yellow-brown, the elm a pale tan, the spars golden in their oil
levels.L1: the oak greying where the sun and spray reach it; blocks darkening where hands and tar touch
levels.L2: silver-grey oak with dark grime in the grain, tar-blackened blocks, spars dull brown with tar streaks
levels.L3: scrubbed and oiled again, the grain standing proud, warm brown; the blocks dark and polished by hands
levels.L4: grey-black wet oak with green algae, open checks, black iron stains; spars grey and checked

deck.title: Holystoned pine deck
deck.what: The spar deck's laid pine (slice 7's Planking: planks, waterways' nibs and pitch seams)
deck.closest_camera_note: a sailor's eye standing on deck

levels.L0: new yellow pine with crisp black pitch seams
levels.L1: scrubbed paler, salt-dry in the sun, tar drips under the rigging
levels.L2: grey and dirty, darker in the gangways' traffic, tar spots and soft seams
levels.L3: holystoned almost white, the grain worn proud between hard seams: a navy's pride
levels.L4: black and green, rotten soft planks, the pitch seams cracked and lifting

refs.note: bare softwood deck boards, unvarnished (a scrubbed deck's colour; a holystoned one is paler)

rope.title: Tarred and untarred hemp
rope.what: The standing rigging and cables in Stockholm tar (black, glossy when fresh), the untarred lanyards and running rigging's hemp, the hammock nettings
rope.closest_camera_note: the shrouds and lanyards at the rail
rope.maps_note: the J-Class's manila fibre map (Inputs/jclass-detail) stands in for hemp's: both long hard fibres of that size

levels.L0: glossy fresh tar, nearly black; the untarred hemp a golden straw
levels.L1: the tar dulled to a deep brown-black; the hemp greying a little
levels.L2: brown tar worn to fibre where it is handled and rubbed, the hemp grey and hairy
levels.L3: re-tarred black with a soft sheen, the hemp renewed: a kept rig
levels.L4: grey bleached tar on top and rotten black below, the hemp dark grey and furred with mildew

canvas.title: Flax canvas
canvas.what: The sails (flax duck, the cloths sewn 2 ft wide), the hammocks' canvas and the tarred tarpaulins over the hatches
canvas.closest_camera_note: the courses' feet over the deck

levels.L0: new buff flax, crisp and even, the seams' double stitching bright
levels.L1: a shade greyer, a little dirt along the foot
levels.L2: dingy grey-buff, grimy along the foot and under the yards, patched with paler new cloths
levels.L3: a newer suit kept dry and clean: pale buff, a few patches
levels.L4: dark grey and black-spotted with mildew, brown stains, many patches

canvas.maps_note: the J-Class's cotton duck mask (Inputs/jclass-detail) stands in for the weave's gaps and tone: the boats' shared Canvas has a normal map only, and a flax canvas's coarser weave is under a pixel past a metre

iron.title: Iron and lead
iron.what: The blacked cast iron of the guns and anchors (lamp black in oil over the iron), the wrought iron fittings (chain plates, bands, eyebolts, hoops) and the hawse holes' lead
iron.closest_camera_note: a gun's breech at the gun deck's crew's eye
iron.maps_note: the J-Class's sand-cast bronze map (Inputs/jclass-detail) is a sand casting's skin: the guns' cast iron has the same

levels.L0: smooth dull black blacking over the iron, the lead bright grey
levels.L1: the black a little brown at the edges, a first orange bloom on the wrought iron
levels.L2: brown rust blooming through the black, orange at the edges and bolts, the lead whitening
levels.L3: freshly blacked again, the casting's skin showing, clean
levels.L4: flaking orange-brown rust all over, the black only in patches, the lead white and pitted

refs.note: black-painted iron rusting through: the blacking neglected

bright.title: Gilt and bronze
bright.what: The carved work's gold leaf (head, stern, quarter galleries) and the bronze (rudder's pintles, the bell, the compass bowls)
bright.closest_camera_note: the quarter gallery's carving from the deck, the bell at the belfry

levels.L0: bright new gold leaf, the bronze new and golden
levels.L1: the gold a shade duller, dirt settling in the carving's hollows
levels.L2: dull gold with dark hollows and chips of red bole showing, the bronze brown
levels.L3: re-gilt bright, the hollows clean; the bronze polished
levels.L4: the gold mostly gone to grey wood and red bole, green verdigris on the bronze

unweathered.Glass: the window panes: cleaned every morning on a navy ship; salt haze on glass is left to the game's own wet look
unweathered.CompassCard: inside the binnacle's glass, out of the weather
unweathered.Shadow: the holes in the deadeyes and blocks: a dark stand-in for shadow, not a surface
unweathered.Clay_Hull: the moulded hull, hidden: the shape tools' reference
unweathered.Deck: slice 2's placeholder deck under the planking, never seen
unweathered.Interior: the gun deck's placeholder inside the ship (slice 2), replaced below decks by slice 12's parts; seen only through a port

below_decks.about: materials of slices 12 to 14 (gun deck, berth deck, orlop and hold), dressed as each lands on main: listed so the outside build's check passes before then

maps.about: Her own map is made by textures.py into Inputs/frigate-detail (plain git, as Inputs/boat-detail); the others are the boats' shared library (Inputs/boat-detail) and the J-Class's (Inputs/jclass-detail). Every map is box-projected in each part's own frame at its real size (tile_mm) and fades out between fade_m metres from the camera.

Oak.note: quarter-sawn and flat-sawn oak and pine together: ring-porous earlywood bands of pores, medullary ray flecks, checks; R grain tone, G checks, B height

Metal.use: the copper sheets' rolled skin, wrought iron

budget.note: her own maps' memory with mips (BC5 normal + BC1 mask); the shared and J-Class maps are already in the game's memory
